title: Canonical regular quotient completion unit criterion
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Assume countable products of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves are exact. Let $a$ be a global section whose multiplication on $\mathcal O$ is injective. For a K-flat cochain complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], put $U_n=P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O/a^n\mathcal O$, restricted to $\mathcal O$, with quotient transitions, and $C_a(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nU_n\to\prod_nU_n)[-1]$. Define $\eta_{a,P}:P\to C_a(P)$ to have product component the quotient maps and zero shifted-product component. Use module-derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Say $N$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete when, for every slice $\mathcal C/V$ and local section $f\in(a)\mathcal O(V)$, $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_V}(\mathcal O_V[1/f],N|_V)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], where localization is sheafified sectionwise. Then $C_a(P)$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete. The following are equivalent: $P$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete; $\eta_{a,P}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O)$; there exists a distinguished Roos triangle $P\xrightarrow{(q_n)}\prod_n^D U_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n^D U_n\to P[1]$ with the prescribed quotient components [def-weil-derived-limit]. These assertions concern the specified zero-component map, not an arbitrarily chosen lift. All tensor products of module sheaves are sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], applied termwise to complexes when an ordinary tensor is written.

proof.text: Every power of multiplication by a is mono. The cone-to-cokernel augmentation of its degree-zero two-term sequence is a quasi-isomorphism by the exact short-complex cone theorem. Tensoring in the K-flat coefficient variable preserves this quasi-isomorphism. The canonical tower comparison is therefore levelwise a quasi-isomorphism. Exact countable products preserve quasi-isomorphisms, and the mapping-cone triangle shows that its strict Roos map is a quasi-isomorphism. This proves the quotient/Koszul Roos isomorphism directly.

In the two strict Roos coordinates, functoriality sends the augmentation (0,gamma) to (0,gamma followed by the tower comparison). The canonical quotient augmentation is exactly this composite. Thus the Koszul/quotient Roos isomorphism carries the actual principal Koszul unit to the actual quotient unit, not merely to a map with the same derived product projections.

The principal Koszul Roos reflector gives completeness of the Koszul Roos complex and bijections on Hom into every locally complete object. Transport completeness to the quotient completion. A reflection unit into a reflective subcategory is invertible exactly when its source belongs to the subcategory: use the Hom bijection to obtain an inverse and its injectivity for the other inverse identity. The unit-compatible Roos isomorphism gives precisely the displayed quotient-unit criterion.

Exact products imply that Q of the termwise complex product is a derived product (DerivedCategory.isLimitFanQ). Conjugating Q(1-s) by the unique product isomorphism gives the derived 1-s, by each product projection. Transport the distinguished mapping-cocone triangle along this product isomorphism. Its first map is Q(roosProj) followed by the product comparison, and its components are Q(roosEval). If the actual quotient unit is invertible, transport the first vertex along it; the strict augmentation identities yield exactly the prescribed quotient components.

Conversely any displayed distinguished quotient Roos triangle has the same two product vertices and second map as the canonical strict Roos triangle. The triangle-morphism completion axiom gives a morphism between first vertices extending identities on both product vertices. The two-out-of-three theorem makes this morphism invertible. Hence P is isomorphic to the locally complete quotient Roos complex, so P is locally complete. The reflection criterion already established makes the specified quotient unit invertible. No arbitrary triangle filler is identified with the canonical unit.

One commit; the statement is unchanged; no new nodes; not on the dropped list; no re-split note; still unsplit in live and side-live, and the six cited statements match live. Step 1 uses the regular Koszul reconstruction with t=a and K-flat P, and its hypotheses hold. Step 2: the last paragraph of the strict Roos comparison (exact countable products, small site) shows that the zero-shifted-component quotient map eta corresponds to the canonical augmentation. Step 1's augmentation compatibility then gives theta∘eta = kappa (the reflector unit). Since a is regular, (a)O(V)=a·O(V), so the item's completeness condition is literally the reflector's for J=(a). Step 3: the reflector gives completeness of Lambda(P) and of C_a(P), and kappa iso iff P complete, hence eta iso iff P complete. Step 4: transport the homotopy-limit Roos triangle along h=rho∘eta (TR1); its components are q_n because rho commutes with the projections. Advisory: that node's statement does not spell out p's components; I accept the standard meaning. Step 5: the second paragraph of Koszul reconstruction gives P ≅ Lambda(P), so P is complete and eta is an isomorphism by Step 3, with no claim that phi equals kappa. The parent lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison uses exactly the proved directions. Sources: I read Stacks 0A0E lemma-derived-completion-koszul, and 0941 is mapped correctly. Edge cases checked: a a unit, O=0, and O=Z, a=p, P=Z. No cycle in the 646-node dependency closure. No duplicate: the pbc actual-completed reconstruction node needs an adic datum.
